LanguageData.CC_God_KnownFrom_void: from its own voice in the dark
LanguageData.CC_God_KnownFrom_sign: from a sign of it on the colony's own land
LanguageData.CC_GW_Feast_Dead: the night of the dead for {GOD}
LanguageData.CC_GW_Slight_Rival_0: We hear you still leave bread out for {THEIRGOD}. {OURGOD} would have more sense than to eat it, but I suppose someone must.
LanguageData.CC_GW_Slight_Rival_1: I will say plainly what my people think of {THEIRGOD}: a god for those who have never met a better one. {OURGOD} has never needed bread on a shelf.
LanguageData.CC_GW_Slight_Rival_2: You may keep {THEIRGOD}, {THEIREPITHET} or whatever you call it these days. We keep {OURGOD}, and we know which of us sleeps better.
LanguageData.CC_GW_Slight_Scoff_0: I confess I have never understood the business with {THEIRGOD}. Grown people bowing to a story, and the bread going stale on the shelf.
LanguageData.CC_GW_Slight_Scoff_1: Please give my regards to {THEIRGOD}, if it ever turns up to collect them.
LanguageData.CC_GW_Slight_Scoff_2: Someone here asked whether {THEIRGOD} would be offended by our letter. I told them a god that minds the post has too much time on its hands.
LanguageData.CC_GW_Slight_Note: {WRITER}'s words about {GOD} will not sit well at {TOWN}.
LanguageData.CC_GW_Slight_Taken: {PEOPLE} took offense at what {WRITER} wrote of {GOD}, and they think the less of the colony for it.
LanguageData.CC_GW_Invite_Text: {PEOPLE} write from {TOWN} that they keep {FEAST} in a few days' time, and that the colony would be welcome at the table of {GOD}, {GODEPITHET}.\n\nThey ask nothing, but a gift for the feast is the custom among neighbors: {COUNT} silver, say, carried out to the gate, where their messenger will take it up the road.
LanguageData.CC_GW_Invite_Ours: {GOD} is one of the colony's own gods, and some of the colony would gladly send something.
LanguageData.CC_GW_Invite_Rival: {GOD} is no friend of {PATRON}, the colony's patron, and a gift to its feast will be noticed by both.
LanguageData.CC_GW_Invite_GiftLabel: the colony's gift for a neighbor's feast
LanguageData.CC_GW_Invite_Why: the colony sent a gift to the feast of {PEOPLE}
LanguageData.CC_GW_Shared: {PEOPLE} think the better of the colony for its standing with {GOD}, whom they also keep.
LanguageData.CC_GW_Feud: {PEOPLE} keep {GOD}, who has no love for {PATRON}, and they think the less of a colony {PATRON} favors.
LanguageData.CC_GW_HolyWar_Label: {PEOPLE} ask for the colony's help in a holy war
LanguageData.CC_GW_HolyWar_Text: {PEOPLE} write that their war with {ENEMY} is no war over land. It is {GOD}'s quarrel with {ENEMYGOD}, {ENEMYEPITHET}, fought by the peoples who keep them, and they ask the colony to stand with them.\n\nStanding with them would warm {PEOPLE} and their god, and cool {ENEMY} and theirs. Sending help, {COUNT} silver carried out to their courier at the gate, is a smaller thing. The colony may also stay out of it.
LanguageData.CC_GW_HolyWar_HelpLabel: the colony's help to a holy war
LanguageData.CC_GW_HolyWar_Why: the colony stood with {PEOPLE} in its holy war
LanguageData.CC_GW_HolyWar_WhyAgainst: the colony stood against it with {PEOPLE}
LanguageData.CC_GW_HolyWar_WhyHelp: the colony sent help to {PEOPLE} in its war
LanguageData.CC_GW_HolyWar_Chronicle: The colony declared for {PEOPLE} in their holy war against {ENEMY}, which they call the quarrel of {GOD}.
LanguageData.CC_GW_Envoy_Label: An envoy of {PEOPLE} asks for a relic
LanguageData.CC_GW_Envoy_Text: {ENVOY_nameDef}, an envoy of the temple of {GOD} among {PEOPLE}, has come to the colony's gate. {ENVOY_pronoun} says the colony holds {RELIC}, which is holy to {GOD}, and asks, with great courtesy, that it come home to the temple.\n\nGiven, {ENVOY_nameDef} will walk to it and carry it away, and {PEOPLE} will not forget it. The colony may instead let {ENVOY_objective} pray over it an hour and keep it, or refuse.
LanguageData.CC_GW_Envoy_Pray: Let the envoy pray over {RELIC}, and keep it
LanguageData.CC_GW_Envoy_WhyGiven: the colony gave {RELIC} back to its temple
LanguageData.CC_GW_Envoy_WhyPrayed: the colony let its envoy pray over {RELIC}
LanguageData.CC_GW_Envoy_Taken: {ENVOY_nameDef} has taken up {RELIC} for the temple of {GOD}, and is carrying it home to {PEOPLE}.
LanguageData.CC_GW_Envoy_PrayedNews: {ENVOY_nameDef} knelt an hour by {RELIC} and prayed to {GOD}, and went home content.
LanguageData.CC_GW_Envoy_Chronicle: The colony gave {RELIC} back to the temple of {GOD} among {PEOPLE}.
LanguageData.CC_GW_Pilgrims_Gone: {SITE} is gone, and the pilgrims of {FACTION} are packing up in grief: {X_nameDef} says {GOD} will hear of it.
LanguageData.CC_GW_Pilgrims_WhyGone: the holy place its pilgrims came to, {SITE}, was destroyed on the colony's land
LanguageData.CC_GW_Pilgrims_Why: its pilgrims prayed at {SITE} on the colony's land in peace
LanguageData.CC_GW_Pilgrims_WhyJoined: the colony prayed with its pilgrims at {SITE}
LanguageData.CC_GW_Pilgrims_Act: pilgrims prayed to {GOD} at {SITE} on the colony's land
LanguageData.CC_GW_Pilgrims_Impact: The pilgrims' god will remember the colony prayed with them.
LanguageData.CC_GW_Seer_Says: {X_nameDef}, the seer at the edge of the land, has spoken at {X_possessive} fire:
LanguageData.CC_GW_Seer_Quarrel: "{A} and {B} are not done with each other, and the sky will show it."
LanguageData.CC_GW_Seer_Grudge: "{GOD} has not forgotten {PAWN}, and it is watching for its moment."
LanguageData.CC_GW_Seer_Hunger: "The hollow one will come for what it is owed, and it always comes."
LanguageData.CC_GW_Seer_Sleeper: "The one in the vault dreams of a door, and the door is a little weaker than it was."
LanguageData.CC_GW_Seer_Angry: "{GOD} is {WORD} with this place, and it does not keep its anger to itself."
LanguageData.CC_GW_Seer_Kind: "{GOD} watches this place kindly, and a god that watches kindly sometimes gives."
LanguageData.CC_GW_Seer_Patron: "{GOD} is {WORD} with you, and the rest are watching to see what you do."
LanguageData.CC_GW_Seer_Nothing: "The gods are quiet here, which is a mercy, or a warning."
LanguageData.CC_GW_Seer_Line: {GOD} is {WORD} with the colony, and is {NATURE} by nature.
LanguageData.CC_GW_Seer_NoneKnown: No god the colony knows has turned its eyes on it yet.
LanguageData.CC_GW_Seer_Impact: The seer reads the colony's standing with each god it knows, and what is coming.
LanguageData.CC_GW_Champion_Text: {GOD} has sent its champion against the colony: {CHAMPION_nameDef} leads this raid of {PEOPLE}, and fights as if a god were watching. If the colony beats {CHAMPION_objective}, it will be a sign.
LanguageData.CC_GW_Champion_WhyGod: its champion {CHAMPION_nameDef} fell before the colony
LanguageData.CC_GW_Champion_WhyRival: the colony beat {CHAMPION_nameDef}, the champion of {OTHER}
LanguageData.CC_GW_Champion_Fell_Dead: {GOD} has seen its champion die: {CHAMPION_nameDef} fell on the colony's land, and the gods who quarrel with {GOD} are pleased.
LanguageData.CC_GW_Champion_Fell_Down: {GOD} has seen its champion beaten: {CHAMPION_nameDef} lies in the dirt of the colony's land, and the gods who quarrel with {GOD} are pleased.
LanguageData.CC_GW_Champion_Fell_Taken: {GOD} has seen its champion taken: {CHAMPION_nameDef} is the colony's captive now, and the gods who quarrel with {GOD} are pleased.
LanguageData.CC_GW_Champion_Chronicle: The colony beat {CHAMPION_nameDef}, the champion {GOD} sent against it.
LanguageData.CC_GW_Beasts_Text: {GOD} sent them: {BEASTS} have come out of the trees and are making straight for {PAWN}, who killed what was sacred to {GOD}. Get {PAWN} inside, or stand with {PAWN_objective}.
LanguageData.CC_GW_Blight_Text: {GOD} is angry with {HOME}, and has turned its face from the fields: a blight is coming over the crops.
LanguageData.CC_GW_Eclipse_Text: {GOD} has turned its back on {HOME} and taken the light with it: the sun has gone dark over the colony for the afternoon.
LanguageData.CC_GW_Field_Text: {GOD} spoke in the storm: lightning struck the open ground by the colony, close enough for everyone to hear what it meant.
LanguageData.CC_GW_Lightning_Roof: {GOD} has not forgotten {PAWN}: the lightning struck straight down onto the roof over {PAWN}'s bed.
LanguageData.CC_GW_Lightning_Near: {GOD} has not forgotten {PAWN}: the lightning struck the ground a few steps from {PAWN}, and nowhere else.
LanguageData.CC_GW_Bless_Fever: {GOD} sat with {PAWN} in the night: the fever broke before dawn, and {PAWN}'s {ILLNESS} is on the turn.
LanguageData.CC_GW_Bless_Plague: {GOD} eased {PAWN}'s plague in the small hours: the sweats are gone, and {PAWN} is sleeping easier.
LanguageData.CC_GW_Gift_Beast: a {BEAST} of its own, tame and bonded
LanguageData.CC_GW_Gift_Path: a psylink and a psycaster's path
LanguageData.CC_GW_Gift_Sculpture: a relic of {GOD}, a small figure in gold
LanguageData.CC_GW_Price_Offering: {COUNT} silver, carried out past the gate and left for the god
LanguageData.CC_GW_Price_Mark: {GOD}'s mark on their skin, for good
LanguageData.CC_GW_Price_Blood: their blood, a cut on the arm given there and then
LanguageData.CC_GW_Price_Label: the price of a god's gift
LanguageData.CC_GW_Price_WhyRival: {PAWN} took a gift of {OTHER}'s, and the price was this god's anger
LanguageData.CC_GW_Offer_Text_Believed: {PAWN} dreamed of {GOD}, {GODEPITHET}, three nights running, and the colony believes it means a gift: {GIFT}.\n\nIn the dream there was a price: {PRICE}. If the colony accepts, {PAWN} will go out under the open sky and wait for it.
LanguageData.CC_GW_Offer_Text_Felt: Some say {GOD}, {GODEPITHET}, has taken an interest in {PAWN}: a voice in the wind offered {PAWN} {GIFT}.\n\nThe voice named its price: {PRICE}. If the colony accepts, {PAWN} will go out under the open sky and wait for it.
LanguageData.CC_GW_Offer_Text_Walking: {GOD}, {GODEPITHET}, has spoken to {PAWN} plainly, in front of everyone: it offers {PAWN} {GIFT}.\n\nIt names its price: {PRICE}. If the colony accepts, {PAWN} will go out under the open sky and wait for it.
LanguageData.CC_GW_Offer_Trickster: {GOD} is a trickster, and its gifts have a way of turning.
LanguageData.CC_GW_Offer_NotNow: {PAWN} is in no state to pay it now.
LanguageData.CC_GW_Gift_Text: {GOD} gave {PAWN} {GIFT} under the open sky, and {PAWN} came back changed.
LanguageData.CC_GW_Gift_Nothing: {GOD} did not come to {PAWN} under the sky after all, and the price was paid for nothing.
LanguageData.CC_GW_Trick_Curse: {GOD} has had its joke: {PAWN}'s gift, {GIFT}, has turned sour, and everything {PAWN} touches goes a little wrong.
LanguageData.CC_GW_Trick_Back: {GOD} has tired of the joke: {PAWN}'s gift, {GIFT}, has come back to {PAWN} as it was.
LanguageData.CC_GW_Undo_Comes: {GOD} has come to the gate, and it wants {OTHER}'s gift to {PAWN} undone.
LanguageData.CC_GW_Undo_Text: {GOD} has come to the colony's gate, walking as one of its people, and it has come for {PAWN}: it will not stand for {OTHER}'s gift, {GIFT}, and means to take it back.\n\nLet it, and it will walk to {PAWN} and take it, and {OTHER} will be the less pleased. Send it away, and {GOD} will go angry.
LanguageData.CC_GW_Undo_WhySent: the colony sent it away from {PAWN}
LanguageData.CC_GW_Undo_WhyLetGo: the colony let it undo a rival's gift to {PAWN}
LanguageData.CC_GW_Undo_WhyLost: the colony let {OTHER} take its gift back from {PAWN}
LanguageData.CC_GW_Undo_Done: {GOD} laid a hand on {PAWN}, and {GIFT} was gone.
LanguageData.CC_GW_Hunger_dying: {GOD} heard {PAWN} dying: a voice from under the world offers to close the wounds and hold back the end, now, if the colony says yes. It names no price. It never does.
LanguageData.CC_GW_Hunger_breaking: {GOD} heard {PAWN} at the edge: a voice from under the world offers {PAWN} stillness, a cold calm that will keep the mind from breaking. It names no price. It never does.
LanguageData.CC_GW_Hunger_starving: {GOD} heard the colony's hunger: a voice from under the world, in {PAWN}'s ear at night, offers meat enough for everyone by morning. It names no price. It never does.
LanguageData.CC_GW_Hunger_Again: It has taken from the colony before, and it always takes more.
LanguageData.CC_GW_Hunger_Act: it answered {PAWN} out of the dark
LanguageData.CC_GW_Hunger_Paid: {GOD} paid at once, as it always does: {PAID} It will come for its due.
LanguageData.CC_GW_Hunger_Mended: {PAWN}'s wounds closed and the fever fell back, as if a cold hand had pressed on them.
LanguageData.CC_GW_Hunger_Stilled: {PAWN}'s mind went still, as cold and quiet as a frozen pond.
LanguageData.CC_GW_Hunger_Fed: {COUNT} {FOOD} lie at the colony's door in the morning, and nobody saw who brought them.
LanguageData.CC_GW_Hunger_Chronicle: {PAWN} took what {GOD} offered out of the dark.
LanguageData.CC_GW_Hunger_Took: {GOD} came for what it was owed: {TOOK}
LanguageData.CC_GW_Hunger_TookMark: {PAWN} woke with the void's mark on {PAWN_objective}, and will carry it.
LanguageData.CC_GW_Hunger_TookYears: {PAWN} woke {YEARS} years older, gray where {PAWN_pronoun} was not.
LanguageData.CC_GW_Hunger_TookHumanity: {PAWN} woke without something {PAWN_pronoun} cannot name, and looks at the others as if they were strangers.
LanguageData.CC_GW_Hunger_TookMind: {PAWN}'s mind has gone wandering where the voice lives.
LanguageData.CC_GW_Hunger_TookBeast: {BEAST} walked into the dark at the edge of the light, and did not come back.
LanguageData.CC_GW_Choir_Text: {PEOPLE} write, in a hand that presses too hard on the page:\n\n"You heard it too. We know, because we hear everything it says. {PAWN} took what {GOD} offered. We will not judge you; we have all been tempted. But it always takes more, and you should keep your halls quiet."
LanguageData.CC_GW_Quarrel_Text: {GOD} and {OTHER}, {OTHEREPITHET}, have fallen out again, as {TIE} do, and the sky over the colony is where they are fighting it: rain and thunder on {GOD}'s days, a hard dry sky on {OTHER}'s, turn and turn about.\n\nThe colony could make an offering to one of them, which would end it sooner in that god's favor and cost it the other's.
LanguageData.CC_GW_Quarrel_Act: it quarreled with {OTHER} in the sky over the colony
LanguageData.CC_GW_Quarrel_Storm: {GOD} has the sky today, and {OTHER} has lost this round: the rain is coming in.
LanguageData.CC_GW_Quarrel_Dry: {GOD} has pushed {OTHER}'s storm off the colony today: the sky is clear and hard.
LanguageData.CC_GW_Quarrel_Over: {GOD} and {OTHER} have finished their quarrel for now, and the weather is the weather again.
LanguageData.CC_GW_Quarrel_WhySide: the colony took its side against {OTHER}
LanguageData.CC_GW_Quarrel_WhySpurned: the colony took {OTHER}'s side against it
LanguageData.CC_GW_Slight_Ask: {GOD} wants something of the colony: that it speak against {OTHER}, out loud, to {PEOPLE} who keep {OTHER}. Do it, and {GOD} will be pleased, and {OTHER} and {PEOPLE} will not.
LanguageData.CC_GW_Ask_WhyRefused: the colony would not do as it asked
LanguageData.CC_GW_Slight_WhyDone: the colony spoke against {OTHER} at its asking
LanguageData.CC_GW_Slight_WhyRival: the colony spoke against it, at {OTHER}'s asking
LanguageData.CC_GW_Slight_News: The colony's word against {OTHER} has gone out on the roads, as {GOD} asked, and {PEOPLE} have heard it.
LanguageData.CC_GW_Hide_Text: {GOD} sent {PAWN_nameDef} of {PEOPLE} to the colony's gate: {OTHER} wants {PAWN_objective} found, and {HUNTERS} are looking. {PAWN_pronoun} asks to be hidden for a few days, until the hunt moves on.\n\nHidden, {PAWN_nameDef} will stay near the colony three days, and {GOD} will be pleased, and {OTHER} will not. Turned away, {PAWN_pronoun} will take {PAWN_possessive} chances on the road.
LanguageData.CC_GW_Hide_WhyHidden: the colony hid {PAWN} at its asking
LanguageData.CC_GW_Hide_WhyTurned: the colony turned away {PAWN}, whom it sent
LanguageData.CC_GW_Hide_Goes: {PAWN} is safe to go home now, and thanks the colony on {GOD}'s behalf.
LanguageData.CC_GW_Term_Text: {GOD} has made the colony an offer, in terms and nothing else: {COUNT} {GOODS}, delivered past the colony's gate within {DAYS} days. In return, {RCOUNT} {REWARD}, from orbit, the day after.\n\nIt will keep its side exactly. It expects the same, and it does not forget a broken word. The colony would carry the goods out as soon as its stores hold them.
LanguageData.CC_GW_Term_Delivered: The colony has carried out {COUNT} {GOODS} for {GOD}'s terms. Its side is due tomorrow.
LanguageData.CC_GW_Term_Kept: {GOD} has kept its side exactly: {RCOUNT} {REWARD} fell from orbit into the middle of the colony.
LanguageData.CC_GW_Term_WhyKept: the colony kept its terms exactly
LanguageData.CC_GW_Term_Broken: {GOD} has noted the term the colony did not keep: {COUNT} {GOODS}, not delivered. It sent nothing, said nothing, and will remember.
LanguageData.CC_GW_DeadMark_Text: {PAWN} found a sign cut into {THING}, worn nearly smooth: the mark of {GOD}, {GODEPITHET}, a god nobody prays to any more. Someone prayed here, long before the colony came.\n\nThe few who still keep {GOD} will be glad to hear it was found.
LanguageData.CC_GW_DeadMark_Why: {PAWN} found its mark in an old place
LanguageData.CC_GW_Fading_Gentle: {GOD}, {GODEPITHET}, has nobody left, and it came to the colony's fires last night like a draught of old air, asking only that someone say its name.\n\nRemember it, and it will be glad of it, in whatever small ways it still can.
LanguageData.CC_GW_Fading_Bitter: {GOD}, {GODEPITHET}, has nobody left, and it is angry about it. It came to the colony's fires last night like a cold wind and demanded to be remembered.\n\nRemember it, and it will be quiet. Refuse, and it will take the light for an afternoon, out of spite.
LanguageData.CC_GW_Fading_WhyRemembered: the colony said its name at the fire
LanguageData.CC_GW_Fading_WhyForgotten: the colony would not remember it
LanguageData.CC_GW_Sleeper_Dream: {GOD} is dreaming in the vault, and {PAWN} has been dreaming with it: a door far below the ground, and a voice behind it, patient and enormous.
LanguageData.CC_GW_Sleeper_Ask_0: The voice asks for {COUNT} {GOODS}, carried out past the gate and left in the dark for it. It does not say what for.
LanguageData.CC_GW_Sleeper_Ask_1: The voice asks the colony to send word to {PEOPLE}, who keep the vault, that their watch is old and tired and the door is not worth keeping. They will not thank the colony for it.
LanguageData.CC_GW_Sleeper_Ask_2: The voice asks for one thing more: that the colony say, out loud and together, that it wishes the door open. It says this is the last thing it will ask.
LanguageData.CC_GW_Sleeper_CarryLabel: what {GOD} asked for in the dream
LanguageData.CC_GW_Sleeper_WhyStep: the colony did what it asked in a dream
LanguageData.CC_GW_Sleeper_WhyRefused: the colony would not do what it asked
LanguageData.CC_GW_Sleeper_StepAct: the colony brought it a step nearer the door
LanguageData.CC_GW_Sleeper_Open: {GOD} has stirred: the door below the vault has opened a crack, and a calm the colony has never felt lies over the land like snow. {PEOPLE}, who kept that door shut for generations, are furious with the colony.
LanguageData.CC_GW_Sleeper_Chronicle: The colony helped open the door below the vault a crack, and {GOD} stirred.
LanguageData.CC_GW_Newborn_Sign_1: {GOD}, the colony's own small god, gave its first sign: a warm wind went through the middle of the colony at dusk, and every fire burned a little brighter.
LanguageData.CC_GW_Newborn_Sign_2: {GOD} is growing: two of the colony dreamed of it the same night, and could tell each other the dream before breakfast.
LanguageData.CC_GW_Newborn_Sign_3: {GOD} answered a small prayer: a little silver lay in the middle of the colony in the morning, where nobody had dropped it.
